Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Firstsource Solutions Limited Q2 
FY27 Earnings Conference Call. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-
only mode and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the 
presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, please

known and unknown risks. These uncertainties and risks include, but are not limited to,

report that are available on its website. 
On this call, we have with us Mr. Ritesh Idnani, MD and CEO; and Mr. Dinesh Jain, 
CFO, to provide an overview on company's performance followed by Q&A. I now hand 
the conference over to Mr. Ritesh Idnani. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Ritesh Idnani: 
Thank you and hello, everybody. Thank you for joining us today to discuss our financial 
results for Q2 FY27. The second quarter reinforces a simple belief that sustainable 
transformation is built on execution. Our clients are navigating change faster than any 
plan can anticipate, and what they want is not another firm telling them what is possible, 
but a partner who will execute alongside them, adapt as conditions change, and stand 
behind the result. Last quarter, I called this accountability. 
This quarter, our focus moved to what makes it repeatable. When we solve a problem 
well once, we should be able to solve it well again for a different client in a different 
market with a different team. That takes systems, not just effort, and those systems are 
built on what our 39,937 Firstsourcers around the world already know. I would like to 
thank each one of them for their relentless commitment to delivering value to our clients.  
Q2 and H1 Performance 
Let me start with the discussion on our Q2 performance. Q2 marks the 10th straight 
quarter of double-digit year-on-year revenue growth and the 12th straight quarter of 
sequential revenue growth. Our revenue grew by 22.2% year-on-year and 3.7% 
quarter-on-quarter and came in at INR 28.3 billion. In US dollar terms, the growth was 
11.7% year-on-year and 2.6% quarter-on-quarter to US$296 million. In constant 
currency terms, our revenue grew 12.3% year-on-year and 2% quarter-on-quarter. 
EBIT margin for the quarter was 12.5%, up 100 basis points year-on-year and 10 basis 
points on a quarter-on-quarter basis, respectively. This is our eighth straight quarter of 
sequential margin expansion. Our net profit was INR2.3 billion and the diluted EPS for 
the quarter was INR3.31. 
In H1 of FY27, our revenue grew 12.3% in constant currency terms. EBIT grew 33.4% 
and our PAT grew 14.3% over last year in rupee terms. 
Business Highlights 
Coming to the business highlights, I will start with our deal wins and other client-related 
metrics. In Q2, we signed four large deals, two of which came from new logos. As you 
are aware, we consider a deal with an ACV of over US$5 million as a large deal. During 
the quarter, we added 17 new logos, one of our highest quarterly additions. It includes 
six strategic logos. 
We define a strategic logo as one where we see the potential of at least US$5 million 
of annual revenue, and we run a structured program to handhold and monitor such 
relationships to grow them at an accelerated pace. I continue to remain encouraged by 
the scale and quality of our wins, reflecting our deep domain expertise, strong 
technology partnerships, and AI-first approach. 
Several of these are transformative programs that ramp up in phases, provide long-
term growth visibility, with revenue conversion occurring over a longer period as key 
milestones are achieved.

Let me now highlight a few of our notable wins during Q2. 
• We expanded our relationship with a leading UK-based MVNO for customer 
experience services across multiple markets, including the transition of their in-
house operations to our offshore delivery centers. 
• One of the top 10 healthcare payers in North America, an existing client, selected 
us for their claims processing. 
• We expanded our relationship with a leading non-profit managed care organization 
in the US across multiple health plan operations. 
• We were also selected by a leading UK and European bank for managed operations 
support services. This, incidentally, is a new logo for us as well. 
• We also won a deal from a leading US-based student loan provider for legal and 
third-party collections. This is also a new logo for us. 
• We won a large deal from a leading digital bank in the US for CX services. 
• We continue to expand our relationship with one of the largest communications and 
media companies in the UK across customer retention, collections, help desk, and 
digital support services. 
 
Vertical commentary 
 
Let me now turn to our vertical performance, starting with banking and financial 
services. In Q2 FY27, our BFS vertical grew 19% year-on-year and 9% sequentially in 
constant currency terms. We added nine new logos during the quarter. Almost every 
conversation in this vertical now starts in the same place: whether AI can be trusted 
inside a regulated process. 
 
It comes up in intelligent operations, in customer servicing, and most of all in financial 
crime and compliance. Our answer rests on the intelligent context framework, part of 
the Kairos operating system, which gives AI the context it needs to work in a live 
operation. The right data, the right permissions, the domain knowledge, and the 
guardrails. AI does the heavy lifting, but a person signs off on anything that affects a 
customer or a regulator. That is what gives clients the confidence to let AI into these 
processes. Within the vertical, growth was broad-based. Consumer debt levels and 
servicing complexity kept demand high. Cost pressure kept clients focused on 
efficiency. 
 
We also executed well on a large BFS engagement won a few quarters ago, and much 
of the headcount we added went into its delivery commitments. We continue to expand 
our footprint with mid-sized banks as well as FinTechs, modernizing onboarding, 
servicing, as well as their collections operations. We exited the quarter with a healthy 
pipeline in the BFS vertical. 
 
In healthcare, our revenues grew 5% year-on-year, but declined 2% sequentially in 
constant currency terms. We added four new logos during the quarter and continue to 
see strong client engagement across both payer and provider markets. Healthcare 
remains a strategic growth pillar for Firstsource, underpinned by our differentiated 
presence across the entire healthcare value chain and our ability to combine deep 
domain expertise with AI-led operations. 
 
On the provider side, rising denials and slower reimbursement are pushing clients 
towards AI-enabled outcome-based revenue cycle management. A dated catalyst is 
also building. From January of 2027, under HR1, Medicaid renewals for expansion 
adults move from annual to six-monthly, phasing in through the year. Our capabilities 
here are well past the pilot stage. 
 
Voice AI is live across our eligibility, patient access, and collections offerings, and 
Denials AI continues to gain traction. We already run Medicaid eligibility at scale, so this 
is extending an operation rather than building one. On the healthcare payer side, we 
delivered several meaningful scope expansions within existing clients. 
 
Plans are working through elevated medical loss ratios and a more volatile enrollment 
cycle, and demand continues to remain healthy across member services, claims,

we continued to broaden our engagement across existing clients through scope 
expansion and greater utilization of our nearshore and offshore delivery footprint. 
 
Clients remain focused on improving customer experience while driving productivity and 
optimizing service costs, and we are increasingly engaged in AI-led transformation 
initiatives spanning customer service, agent assist, automation, and service assurance. 
Overall, we exited the quarter with a healthy pipeline across our telecom, cable, media, 
technology, and digital-native clients, giving us confidence in the medium-term growth 
trajectory of the business. 
 
And finally, our diverse portfolio, comprising of our utilities and our retail business grew 
25% year-on-year and was flat sequentially in constant currency terms with two new 
logos added during the quarter. In utilities, clients remain focused on cost optimization 
and near shore delivery, while underlying demand and pipeline activity remain healthy. 
 
We also continue to see cross-sell opportunities across customer operations, 
collections and AI-led transformation initiatives within our existing client base. In retail, 
demand remains steady, with clients focused on enhancing customer experience, while 
improving operational efficiency.  
Overall, we exited the quarter with a healthy pipeline across both utilities and retail 
supporting our growth outlook for the segment. 
Geographical commentary 
From a geographic standpoint, North America grew 6% year-on-year and 1% 
sequentially in constant currency terms. Growth was led by BFS, while healthcare 
reflected the timing of certain program ramps and transitions that we have discussed 
earlier. More importantly, client conversations across the region continue to be centered 
on AI-led transformation, productivity improvement and operating model modernization. 
We are seeing growing demand for solutions that combine technology, AI and 
operations expertise and our differentiated capabilities across key verticals position us 
well to participate in these opportunities. We continue to maintain a healthy pipeline and 
remain confident in the medium-term growth outlook for the region. 
Europe delivered another strong quarter, with revenues growing 27% year-on-year and 
7% sequentially in constant currency terms. Growth was led by BFS, with good 
momentum also emerging in CMT. Our largest client relationships remain healthy and 
we are increasingly engaging with them on different transformation initiatives, reflecting 
both the strength of our execution and the relevance of our capabilities. We continue to 
see strong demand for near-shore delivery, particularly from South Africa, supported by 
our transformation-led value proposition. We secured two large wins during the quarter 
and with a healthy and growing pipeline, we remain optimistic about the region's growth 
trajectory.  
Australia delivered a strong quarter, with revenue growing 50% year-on-year, 
supported by continued momentum across existing relationships and a steadily 
improving pipeline.

People 
On the people front, we continued advancing our intelligence-that-operates strategy, 
building a future-ready workforce through disciplined hiring, stronger workforce 
intelligence and AI-enabled people operations. We closed Q2 of FY27 with 39,937 
Firstsourcers, a net increase of 3,062 during the quarter. 
This growth was driven by the transition of associates from a major banking client, 
alongside program ramp-ups predominantly in our offshore and near-shore delivery 
geographies, with India and the Philippines accounting for more than 85% of the 
increase. Together, these reflect growth on both fronts, clients entrusting us with a 
broader share of their operations and our ability to transform how that work gets done 
using technology.  
Voluntary attrition for associates with more than 180 days of tenure remains steady at 
28.4% on a trailing 12-month basis. We remain focused on a range of retention and 
engagement interventions designed to enhance employee experience. We're also 
expanding the use of AI and predictive insights across our people operations, from 
talent acquisition and employee engagement to internal mobility and retention.  
Talent assessments, deeper insights into employee exits via interactive bots and 
forward-looking visibility into attrition risk are enabling earlier, more targeted 
interventions. In parallel, Unbound, our AI-enabled internal talent marketplace is 
strengthening skills-based mobility and creating clearer career pathways for our people.  
Together, these initiatives bring our bold tech to life within our own organization, 
combining AI-led analytics with timely human intervention to strengthen workforce 
stability. 
Awards/recognitions 
During the quarter, our work continued to earn external recognition. 
• HFS featured Firstsource in its non-linearity index as one of the leaders in the shift 
to services-as-software and named us as first runner-up for best services eating 
software at its inaugural services as software awards.  
• HFS also recognized Firstsource as the Horizon 3 market leader for customer 
experience services in 2026. 
• Firstsource was also recognized as a leader across generative AI and agentic AI 
services in the ISG provider lens evaluations, underscoring the strength of our AI-
led transformation offerings. 
• ISG also placed us in the breakthrough 15 in the USD 1-3 billion tier based on the 
deal wins that we secured. 
 
Our people strategy also continued to earn strong external recognition.  
• Firstsource was named among Great Place To Work's Top 50 India's Best 
Workplaces for Women 2026 for the second consecutive year, reinforcing our 
commitments and progress we are making in attracting and retaining female talent. 
• Our investments in people manager capability and employee experience were 
recognized through the Brandon Hall Gold Award for the best development program 
for frontline managers and the Brandon Hall Silver Award for best employee 
engagement. 
Collectively, these recognitions demonstrate the strength of our employee value 
proposition and our ability to attract, engage, and develop the diverse, digitally skilled 
talent needed to deliver our bold tech agenda.

I will come back to talk about our progress on the strategic priorities and the outlook for 
the remainder of FY27.

Progress on strategic priorities + outlook 
Ritesh Idnani:  
Thank you, Dinesh. 
Let me spend a few minutes on a strategic priority that sits at the heart of how we are 
building the next phase of the Firstsource journey. Over the last 25 years, we built deep 
expertise by solving complex problems across industries, clients, and workflows. The 
opportunity before us now is how to make that expertise travel further. How do we take 
what thousands of people have learned and turn it into capabilities that can be shared, 
scaled, continuously improved, and applied wherever they create value. 
That is the thinking behind our shift from services to productized services. 
 
To be clear, this is not about moving away from services, nor is it simply about 
automating what we do today. It's about changing how we package, deliver, and scale 
the expertise we have built. Today, the best way to solve a problem often resides with 
a specific team or within a specific engagement. Productization gives that expertise a 
way to travel through repeatable workflows, embedded AI, and human judgment applied 
where it matters most.

Kairos, our AI-native operating system, serves as the engine for delivering, measuring, 
and scaling productized services. 
 
Our domain harness captures the skills, playbooks, and compliance guardrails of our 
best operators once and makes them available to our people and AI agents alike, 
portable across the models and platforms that our clients choose. 
 
Our intelligent context framework gives AI the memory behind every decision, and 
Kairos learns from how work is done so it gets stronger the longer we operate.  
Governed autonomy is what makes this work in regulated industries, where every 
decision is fully explainable and stays within compliance boundaries that no agent can 
override. Autonomy is earned one task at a time based on evidence, and our people 
progress from doing the work to supervising it to reviewing only the exceptions. 
As we progress on this journey, there are three indicators that we will be watching 
closely. 
 
First, the repeatability of these solutions across clients. The true test of productization 
is not the success of the first deployment, but whether the second, third, or 20th 
deployment becomes easier, faster, and more efficient. 
 
Second, the evolution of our revenue mix. Today, more than 50% of our revenues are 
already non-linear in nature, which we understand is an industry-leading metric. As we 
continue to productize our capabilities, our objective is to further increase the share of 
non-linear, outcome-based, platform-led, and value-linked revenues over time. 
Ultimately, success for us is not just about growing revenue, but about changing the 
shape and quality of that revenue. 
 
And third, disciplined measurement. While AI is generating significant excitement 
across the industry, sustainable value requires clear baselines, rigorous metrics, and 
tangible outcomes. We remain committed to measuring the progress thoughtfully and 
transparently. 
 
Ultimately, the objective is simple. We're taking the expertise, operational knowledge, 
and industry experience that Firstsource has built over 25 years and making it more 
scalable through AI, platforms, and productized delivery. We believe this will strengthen 
our differentiation, deepen client relationships, and expand our long-term growth 
opportunity. 
The next version of Firstsource will not be built by leaving behind what made us 
successful. It will be built by making everything we have learned work harder. 
 
Let me close with the numbers behind the story. 
We ended the quarter with 51 clients generating over $5 million in revenue run rate, six 
more than last quarter, the largest sequential addition in this cohort on an organic basis 
or over the past 5 quarters. We added 3 clients to our $10 million plus cohort, taking 
the total to 23. 
 
The 2 year trend is where the signal is the clearest. Over that period, our $5 million plus 
clients have almost doubled and our $10 million plus clients are up nearly 80%. That is 
the strongest evidence of deepening of the wallet as our clients are giving us more of 
their business and more of the work that matters most to them. 
 
Underneath that, our $1 million plus clients are up 32% during the same time period, a 
broad base that keeps feeding the large relationships of tomorrow. Think of it as each 
cohort feeding the next, and this is by design. Over the last 8 quarters, the revenue 
share of our top 5 and top 10 clients has come down by 6 and 10 percentage points 
respectively. 
 
Importantly, that is not because our largest clients are shrinking. Our top five 
relationships go back over 22 years on average, and they continue to grow at industry 
rate, even with the significant onshore to nearshore and offshore shift in at least a 
couple of them. We are also winning more large deals and winning them more 
consistently.

Outlook for FY27 
That brings me to our outlook for FY27. Based on our H1 performance and the visibility 
we have for the second half, we are raising the lower end of our FY27 revenue 
guidance. 
 
We now expect constant currency revenue growth of 10.5% to 13%, compared with 
10% to 13% earlier. On margins, we are reaffirming our EBIT margin guidance of 
12.25% to 12.75%. This revision reflects the underlying strength and breadth of our 
portfolio. 
Large deals signed over the last few quarters are ramping as planned, our pipeline 
remains healthy, and new logo momentum continues to build, all of which give us 
greater confidence in our growth for the second half. We believe this places us 
comfortably in the top decile of growth in our industry.  
This concludes our opening remarks and we can now open the floor for questions.
